title: Track Pacing Robot
summary: A 1/10-scale robot that follows the lane line at a programmed pace so a runner can chase it.
problem: Without a pacer, runners go out too fast and fade, and only learn how far off they were after the rep. As a cross-country runner I wanted an objective, portable pacer that holds a speed, switches between work and recovery on its own, and sets up from a phone.
approach: The system is split by timescale. An Arduino runs a 100 Hz PID speed loop from an encoder on the rear axle, damps steering with a gyro, and drops to neutral if commands stop for 500 ms. A Raspberry Pi running ROS 2 handles OpenCV lane following, workout segments and the phone interface. A sensored brushless motor and a 9:1 belt reduction put race pace at mid-throttle, so the controller always has headroom.
result: Hardware is selected and documented, the ESC is calibrated, and the firmware and ROS 2 nodes are drafted while the chassis is modeled in Fusion for 3D printing. Pacing accuracy will be measured lap by lap on a real track before I claim it.
